[[ファイル:Tsukiyomi Jinja Kyotanabe Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Torii}}]]
'''Tsukiyomi Shrine''' (つきよみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kyōtanabe|Q816728|qid=Q816728}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288|qid=Q134917288}} and is known as the birthplace of '''{{ill|Hayato-mai|Q55529681|qid=Q55529681}}'''.

=== History ===
=== Outline ===
According to shrine tradition, when the shrine buildings were moved from Heijō-kyō to Heian-kyō in {{ill|809|Q30671|qid=Q30671}} (Daidō 4), divine light was seen on Mt. Ōsumi, and building a shrine at this place marks the founding. During the {{ill|Battle of Toba–Fushimi|Q1193959|qid=Q1193959}}, {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|Q710098|qid=Q710098}} was temporarily relocated here to avoid warfare, and sacred treasures were placed in Yakushi Hall.

=== Court rank ===
*{{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} 3 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), {{ill|January 27|Q2284|qid=Q2284}}: from Junior Fifth Lower to Senior Fifth Lower (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'') - written as "Kabai Tsukuyomi-no-Kami"
*{{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 6 ({{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}}): Junior First Rank (shrine tradition)

=== Hayato-mai ===
[[ファイル:Hyatomai Denshouti.jpg|thumb|150px|{{center|Monument of the birthplace of Hayato-mai}}]]
From a tradition that Ōsumi {{ill|Hayato people|Q1151764|qid=Q1151764}} from southern {{ill|Kyushu|Q13987|qid=Q13987}} migrated to Ōsumi in the {{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}}, and that these Ōsumi Hayato dedicated and transmitted Hayato-mai here, this shrine is regarded as the birthplace of Hayato-mai. At the eve of the annual festival on {{ill|October 14|Q2922|qid=Q2922}}, Hayato-mai is still dedicated (designated an intangible folk cultural property of Kyōtanabe City<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title="Tsukiyomi Shrine and Hayato-mai"|url=http://www.kyotanabe.jp/html/kanko/i/tsukiyomi.htm|website=Kyōtanabe City|accessdate=2019-09-20|language=ja|last=Kyōtanabe City}}</ref>).

Also, the place name "Ōsumi" where this shrine is located is thought to derive from "{{ill|Ōsumi Province|Q981002|qid=Q981002|lt=Ōsumi}}" in Kyushu<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Ōsumi Hayato-mai|url=http://www.kyotanabe.ed.jp/nc24/culture/htdocs/mu6y5636h-117/|website=www.kyotanabe.ed.jp|accessdate=2020-07-03|publisher=Kyōtanabe City Board of Education}}</ref>.
